description.purpose: A place to put rows, as one `store` cell: one declared table and a query timeout, and nothing else. Eighteen shipped templates carry a `store` INSIDE them; none was instantiable on its own (GH #482). It holds, it decides nothing: WHAT goes on it is the `schema` an instance declares, WHO may write is the edge the parent draws.
description.use_when: Whenever something a colony produces has to outlive the message that produced it. Instantiate it under a name that says what it keeps (`headlines`, `receipts`, `seen`) and give it its shape in the SAME declaration: `override_params` carrying a `schema`, a FLAT params object. Then draw the edges -- see RETURN.
description.not_in_scope: No policy, no schedule, no trim, no opinion about the contents. Constraints are not shippable -- a column is `text`, `int` or `json`, and PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE and NOT NULL are core defers of the cell type -- so a duplicate row is a question for whoever writes, not an error the shelf raises.
examples: PORTS - Entry: one message carrying one or more tool_call turns whose text is the JSON args of a store operation (`insert`, `select`, `update`, `delete`, `create_table`, `search`). Exit: ONE answer per message -- a tool_result turn per operation in call order, with `operation`, `rows_affected` and `duration_ms` on the hop, plus `bundle_errors` and a `results[]` slot as soon as the message carried more than one call. A READ's turn TEXT is a bare JSON ARRAY of row objects, never `{"rows": [...]}`. An SQL error rides in a regular tool_result as `error_code`, never a crash.

ARGS - beside `operation` and `table` each operation reads keys of its OWN, and an unread key is REFUSED, not ignored (`unknown argument`, naming the whole set). `insert` takes `row` -- an object, NOT `values`. `select` takes `columns`, `where`, `order_by`, `limit`, `distinct`; `update` takes `set` and `where`; `delete` takes `where`; `create_table` takes `columns`; `search` takes `match` beside the `select` keys. Worked: {"operation": "insert", "table": "headlines", "row": {"id": "a1", "title": "a headline"}} and {"operation": "select", "table": "headlines", "columns": ["id"], "where": {"id": "a1"}}.

RETURN - a store answers EVERY message, and the answer's `hop` is the STORE's own: `hop` is single-hop and REPLACED on every emission, so a `route` stamped outbound is gone; `context` is persistent, so it is IDENTICAL on both legs. `hop.operation` is the only field that names the leg, so a return edge is guarded POSITIVELY on it: [{"from": "./shelf", "to": "./dedupe", "condition": "has(hop.operation) && hop.operation == 'select'"}, {"from": "./shelf", "to": "./dedupe", "default": true}] -- the guard takes the READ answer back, the default takes every other answer (a write says `insert`, or `bundle` above one call) so it does not dead-letter as `no_route`. Guard on `context` and BOTH legs match: the insert answer re-enters the insert branch and the pair loops to the TTL (GH #521).
